Signup and password-reset REQUESTS also verified to reach Supabase correctly (confirmed directly with a bare supabase-js call outside the app) but both attempts during this test session hit Supabase's default email rate limit (`over_email_send_rate_limit`, 429) — the built-in test SMTP on a fresh/free Supabase project allows only a handful of emails per hour, and this session's testing (multiple signups/resets in quick succession) burned through it. This is expected free-tier infrastructure behavior, not an app bug: the action caught it gracefully and returned an error rather than crashing. BUG FOUND: visiting the real confirmation/recovery link lands on `/id/login?error=confirm_failed#access_token=...&refresh_token=...&type=signup` — Supabase's own hosted `/auth/v1/verify` endpoint (what the DEFAULT email templates link to via `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`) verifies the token itself and redirects back with the session in a URL **fragment** (`#access_token=...`), not as `token_hash`/`type` query params. URL fragments are never sent to the server — `src/app/auth/confirm/route.ts` (a server Route Handler) structurally cannot see them, no matter how it's written; this is a browser platform limitation, not a code bug. My route handler correctly implements Supabase's *recommended* SSR pattern (verify `token_hash` server-side via `verifyOtp`), but that pattern only activates if the EMAIL TEMPLATES in the Supabase Dashboard are customized to link to `{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/confirm?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=...` instead of the default `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`. This is a Dashboard-only setting (Authentication → Email Templates) that I cannot change — no Management API token, only the anon/service-role REST keys. ACTION NEEDED FROM USER: in the Supabase Dashboard, edit the 'Confirm signup' template's link to `{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/confirm?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=signup&next=/login%3Fconfirmed%3D1` and the 'Reset Password' template's link to `{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/confirm?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=recovery&next=/reset-password`. Also confirm 'Site URL' under Authentication → URL Configuration is set to `http://localhost:3000` for local dev.
